decisions.mark: states BOTH halves of the contrast: that nothing in library/ creates a thread, AND that library/ nonetheless supplies the mutex abstraction used by threaded callers
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The library spawns nothing, so under default settings it runs on whatever threads the caller provides." and "With both off, `library/threading.c` ... compiles to nothing" plus the lock table showing `library/threading.c` declaring `mbedtls_threading_*_mutex` and "`MBEDTLS_THREADING_C` ... then they protect a small set of library globals plus the heap." | WHY: The answer states that the library spawns no threads (all spawn sites are in programs/) and that library/threading.c supplies the mutex abstraction and locks used by threaded callers. || QUOTE: The library spawns nothing, so under default settings it runs on whatever threads the caller provides. ... `library/threading.c` ... `mbedtls_threading_key_slot_mutex` ...
